Let me analyze this certificate carefully.

Certificate details:
- Number: R49-1/2006-NL1-11.03
- Project number: 11200755
- Page 1 of 4 → page_total: 4
- Member State: The Netherlands
- Issuing authority: NMi Certin B.V., OIML Issuing Authority NL1
- Person responsible: C. Oosterman, Head Certification Board
- Address: Hugo de Grootplein 1, 3314 EG Dordrecht, the Netherlands
- Phone: +31 78 6332332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl
- Website: www.nmi.nl
- Date issued: 22 November 2011 → 2011-11-22
- oiml_issuer_id: NL1

Applicant: Itron, Eau et Energie Thermique, 11 Boulevard Pasteur, 67500 Haguenau, France

Manufacturer: same

Certified type:
- Category: Water meter
- Type designations: ["Sharpflow SOPX+CXP3"]
- Description: Water meter intended for metering cold potable water, based on an electromagnetic principle, designed to measure reverse flow, with straight inlet and outlet length, with no flow conditioner and equipped with an electronic calculating/indicating device.

Recommendation:
- R49, edition 2006 (int)
- scheme: not specified explicitly. The schema has scheme in certificate and recommendation. The certificate number format "R49-1/2006" — the "-1" might indicate scheme... Actually OIML basic scheme vs supplementary. Hard to say. I'll omit scheme unless clear. Actually scheme field in certificate: "scheme (A|B)". Not indicated, so omit.

Model family: The cert covers 7 meter sizes: DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100, DN150, DN250, DN500. So model_family models: DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100, DN150, DN250, DN500.

Matrix tables: Two tables (page 3 and page 4). Combine? Better to emit two matrix_tables entries, or one combined? The schema allows matrix_tables[]. I'll emit two entries: "Metrological characteristics by meter size (DN25–DN100)" and "Metrological characteristics by meter size (DN150–DN500)". Actually could combine into one with all 7 sizes. But safer to preserve as two tables as in the document.

Characteristics model_level (combining both tables):
- minimum_flow_rate_q1: DN25: 0.040, DN50: 0.10, DN80: 0.25, DN100: 0.4, DN150: 0.6, DN250: 1.6, DN500: 12.6 — unit m³/h
- transitional_flow_rate_q2: 0.064, 0.16, 0.40, 0.6, 1.0, 2.6, 20.2 — m³/h
- permanent_flow_rate_q3: 16, 40, 160, 250, 400, 1600, 6300 — m³/h
- overload_flow_rate_q4: 20, 50, 200, 312.5, 500, 2000, 7875 — m³/h
- nominal_diameter: 25, 50, 80, 100, 150, 250, 500 — mm
- accuracy_class: DN25: 2, DN50: 2, DN80: 1, DN100: 1, DN150: 1, DN250: 1, DN500: 1
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 16 bar (all) — could be type_level since constant
- min/max admissible temperature: 0.1 / 50 °C → this is a range 0.1 to 50, type_level. Note "0,1 / 50" — min 0.1, max 50. Unit °C. Interesting: minimum admissible temperature 0.1°C (cold potable water meter). So {min: 0.1, max: 50}.
- indicating_range: DN25: 99.999? Careful: "99.999" with dot as thousands separator (European style) — indicating range 99.999 m³ means 99999 m³. Since footnote says programmable, minimum indicating range. The values: DN25/DN50: 99.999 (i.e., 99,999 = 99 999), DN80/DN100: 999.999 = 999999, DN150: 999.999 = 999999, DN250: 9.999.999 = 9999999, DN500: 99.999.999 = 99999999. These are European-formatted numbers with dots as thousand separators. Hmm. Should I convert? The unit is m³. The values are display maximums. I think converting to integers is right: 99999, 999999, 9999999, 99999999. But there's ambiguity. Given the pattern (11-digit totalizator), these are clearly 99 999, 999 999, etc. I'll use integers.

But wait — is indicating range model_level? Yes, it varies by model. DN25 & DN50: 99999; DN80 & DN100: 999999; DN150: 999999; DN250: 9999999; DN500: 99999999.

- verification_scale_interval: DN25 & DN50: 0.0001 m³; DN80 & DN100: 0.001; DN150 & DN250: 0.001; DN500: 0.01. Unit m³.
- Orientation: All positions — type_level (string value).
- Environmental class: C — type_level.
- Power supply: varies but by power supply type (AC vs DC), not by meter size. In both tables, the power supply rows are: Type mains AC (for some sizes) and DC; Umax 230 V / 24 V; Umin 100 V / 12 V; Frequency 50–60 Hz / "-". This is a configuration axis: power_supply_type. Use config_level:
  - attribute: maximum_supply_voltage (Umax), axis: power_supply_type, values: [{condition: "mains AC", value: 230, unit V}, {condition: "DC", value: 24, unit V}]
  - minimum_supply_voltage (Umin): AC 100 V, DC 12 V
  - supply_frequency: AC {min 50, max 60} Hz; DC null/"-" — for DC frequency not applicable; omit DC condition or value "not applicable". Rules say empty strings not values; use null or omit. I'll include condition DC with value null? Hmm, better to omit DC. Or record only AC. I'll include both conditions, DC with value null — actually cleaner: just AC condition.

For which columns does AC apply? On page 3 table: Type row: "mains AC" colspan=2 (DN25, DN50), "DC" (colspan... alignment: last cell DN100). Actually the header row has 5 cells: Meter size, DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100. The power supply rows have: rowspan cell "Power supply", then "Type", then colspan=2 "mains AC" (DN25, DN50), then "DC" (DN100)? Wait, that leaves DN80 ambiguous. Hmm: rowspan=4 Power supply, Type (1 cell), colspan=2 mains AC, DC — total columns: 1 (power supply) + 1 (Type) + 2 (mains AC) + 1 (DC) = 5. So DN25+DN50: mains AC; then DC covers DN80 and DN100? Only one column left for two headers... Actually with colspan: row = Power supply(rowspan4) | Type | mains AC(colspan2) | DC. Columns: PS, Type, col3+col4 (mains AC), col5 (DC). So mains AC applies to DN25, DN50 and DC applies to DN100 only — DN80? Mismatch. Hmm, the original PDF likely has: mains AC spanning DN25-DN50, DC spanning DN80-DN100? But GLM-OCR shows DC not colspan=2. On page 4: header has 4 cells: Meter size, DN150, DN250, DN500. Power rows: Type | mains AC | DC → 1+1+1+1 = 4? Row: Power supply (rowspan) | Type | mains AC | DC — that's 4 columns: PS, Type label... wait no, that's 4 cells total = PS, "Type", "mains AC", "DC" covering DN150, DN250, DN500? That leaves label column unaccounted. Hmm the page 4 table has no explicit label column? Row 1: Meter size | DN150 | DN250 | DN500 (4 cells). Power row: Power supply(rowspan) | Type | mains AC | DC → 4 cells. So "Type" occupies label position, mains AC → DN150, DC → DN250, and DN500 → ??? Missing. Actually maybe: Type label, mains AC (colspan?) ... OCR is imperfect. Probably intent: mains AC applies to some sizes, DC to others, but exact column mapping is fuzzy. For page 4, likely mains AC spans DN150+DN250? No—there's no colspan shown. Hmm: 4 cells: PS(rowspan), Type, mains AC, DC. If "Type" is the label in first data column, then DN150=mains AC, DN250=DC, DN500=? Unmapped. But both DN250 and DN500 columns... The page 3 table: PS | Type | mains AC (colspan 2) | DC → DN25, DN50 = mains AC; DN80?? 

Given OCR ambiguity, safest: config_level with axis "power_supply_type" and conditions "mains AC" and "DC", without mapping to specific meter sizes. The power supply specs: AC: Umin 100 V, Umax 230 V, 50–60 Hz; DC: Umin 12 V, Umax 24 V. This is consistent across tables.

So:
config_level:
1. {attribute: "maximum_supply_voltage", axis: "power_supply_type", values: [{condition: "mains AC", value: 230, unit_symbol: "V"}, {condition: "DC", value: 24, unit_symbol: "V"}]}
2. {attribute: "minimum_supply_voltage", axis: "power_supply_type", values: [{condition: "mains AC", value: 100, unit_symbol: "V"}, {condition: "DC", value: 12, unit_symbol: "V"}]}
3. {attribute: "power_supply_frequency", axis: "power_supply_type", values: [{condition: "mains AC", value: {min: 50, max: 60}, unit_symbol: "Hz"}]}

But wait — power_supply_type itself varies: values "mains AC" and "DC". Could be type_level: power_supply_type: ["mains AC", "DC"]. Hmm, type_level must be single value. I could put config: {attribute: "power_supply_type", axis: "power_supply_type", values: [{condition: "mains AC", ...}]} — awkward. Maybe simplest: config_level entry with attribute "power_supply" and axis... Actually I'll just record voltage/frequency config entries as above, and that implicitly conveys both AC and DC types. Or add type_level "power_supply_types": {value: "mains AC or DC"}? Rules say single value. I could set value "mains AC / DC" as string. That seems fine and informative. I'll add type_level: power_supply: {value: "mains AC / DC"} — hmm. Let me instead do config_level:

{attribute: "power_supply_type", axis: "power_supply_type", values: [{condition: "mains AC", value: "mains AC"}, {condition: "DC", value: "DC"}]} — redundant. Skip; the voltage/frequency entries have conditions that already name the type.

Actually, maybe cleaner: config_level with axis "power supply variant". I'll name axis "power_supply_type" with conditions "mains AC" and "DC".

Type-level characteristics:
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 16, bar
- admissible_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 50}, °C. Label: "min_max_admissible_temperature" → canonical: admissible_temperature? I'll use "admissible_temperature" with range value. Or "minimum_maximum_admissible_temperature". I'll go "admissible_temperature".
- orientation: "All positions"
- environmental_class: "C"
- totalizator_display_digits: 11 (including 1 decimal digit) — from footnote 3/6: "The display of the totalizator has 11 digits (including 1 digit for the decimal sign". This is in a footnote. Could extract as footnote only. I'll keep as footnotes.

Footnotes: markers [1]-[3] page 3, [4]-[6] page 4. [1]≡[4], [2]≡[5], [3]≡[6] same text. I'll extract with markers "1)", "2)", "3)", "4)", "5)", "6)"? Or dedupe? Schema: footnotes[]: marker, text. I'll list all six as they appear, preserving markers. Or dedupe to three noting they apply to both tables. I'll list all six as in document.

footnote_markers on values: indicating_range values → ["1)","3)"] for DN25/DN50 etc. Use the markers as given in brackets: "[1][3]"? Schema example uses "1)". Footnote example in rules: "footnote_markers": ["1)"]. I'll use "1)" format. For page-4 values markers "4)" and "6)". Hmm, but since dedupe... I'll keep per-table markers as printed: DN25/DN50 indicating range: ["1)","3)"]; DN80/DN100: ["1)","3)"]; DN150: ["4)","6)"]; DN250: ["4)","6)"]; DN500: ["4)","6)"]. Verification scale interval: ["2)","3)"] for DN25/50; ["2)","3)"] DN80/100; ["5)","6)"] DN150/250/500.

Test reports:
- id: R49-1/2003-NL1-06.01, pages 41, role: type_evaluation_report (it's the OIML Test Report). The annexes: Annex A 1 page, Annex 1: 21 pages, ... Annex 17: 26 pages. How to represent? test_reports[] entries with id, pages, role. Main: role "type_evaluation_report", pages 41. Annexes: role "documentation_file"? They're all part of the test report. Options: each annex as separate entry with id "R49-1/2003-NL1-06.01 Annex A", pages, role "test_report" or "documentation_file". I'll list main report plus annexes with role "documentation_file"? Hmm, they're annexes to the test report — I'd say role "test_report" for annexes too, or a distinct role. The enum in schema: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. I'll use "type_evaluation_report" for the main and "documentation_file" for annexes... Actually annexes of test report are test report content. I'll use "test_report" for the annexes. Hmm. Let me use "type_evaluation_report" for the main report and "test_report" for annexes. That's reasonable.

Annex list:

The power supply rows in the table are config-level; including them in matrix rows would be messy. The schema example matrix_tables has columns and rows (object per row). model_family: family_name: null? "Sharpflow" is arguably the family name. The type is "Sharpflow SOPX+CXP3". Family name "Sharpflow" seems reasonable — the cert type designation. Fix "a electromagnetic" → "an electromagnetic"? Keep as-is mostly; minor fix acceptable. I'll write "based on an electromagnetic principle".

- "3)": "The display of the totalizator has 11 digits (including 1 digit for the decimal sign. The format..." I'll keep close to source; slight fix to balance parentheses is fine.
- "4)", "5)", "6)" same texts.

Roles: main → "type_evaluation_report"; Annex A → hmm, Annex A in OIML test reports is typically the documentation/results summary. Role enum: I'll assign "type_evaluation_report" for main, "test_report" for annexes. Fine.

Recommendation: {"id": "R49", "edition": 2006, "accuracy_classes": [1, 2]}. Also scheme? The cert number contains "-1" but that's part of numbering. Omit scheme in recommendation; certificate scheme omit too.

Now JSON output. Ensure numbers as numbers, decimal points. Values 0.040 → 0.04; 0.10 → 0.1; 0.40 → 0.4; 1,0 → 1.0 (JSON 1.0 is fine, will parse as 1.0; could write 1.0). 312.5.

Let me build the final JSON.

config_level values shape: {condition, value, unit_symbol} — the schema says "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}". OK.

Also maybe add config_level for power_supply_type? I'll add an entry:
{"attribute": "power_supply_type", "axis": "power_supply_type", "values": [{"condition": "mains AC", "value": "mains AC"}, {"condition": "DC", "value": "DC"}]} — redundant but harmless; I'll skip it to keep clean. One more check: min/max admissible temperature "0,1 / 50" — value {min: 0.1, max: 50}, unit °C. Good.

Matrix table rows also include temperature as range object. Fine.
